feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector depth. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, culminating in enterprise ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: named platforms/tools, large-scale website migration, audience size, and recent AI/search work make the profile feel current and substantive.  
- Writing is generally polished and consistent in tone, with effective use of action verbs and domain-specific language.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage is mixed but acceptable; “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No obvious misspellings or major grammatical errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear public-sector relevance, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one or two concrete signals of scale would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with sharper action language: “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Add a scale cue from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Reduce the long list of functions; group related areas to improve flow and avoid sounding like a skills dump.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, governance, analytics, editorial operations, and multimedia systems for mission-driven organizations, including large-scale Drupal platforms, cross-functional publishing teams, and emerging AI-enabled content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes multiple skills sections; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “communications” unevenly.
- Prioritize the strongest, most current differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, AI-enabled search, and automation/integration.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If targeting more technical roles, swap “Public-sector advocacy communications” for “CMS and digital platform delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases from the header, especially “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled user experiences.”
- Overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; consider using this section for higher-level themes only.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Tighten parallel structure: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns.
- Clarify specificity where possible: “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot”; consider “AI chat at the bill level” for smoother phrasing.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search — Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a modular architecture for future expansion…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search overlaps with the current freelance role.
- Advocacy Video Series and campaign/microsite work echo NACo and consultant bullets; keep only projects not already clear elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and analytics.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by streamlining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-team publishing processes.
- Established governance and usability standards across web, email, social, and multimedia channels to improve consistency and execution.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time saved, adoption, engagement lift, search success.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the summary and NACo role—avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level scope from your earlier NACo roles. Emphasize transformation, team/operating ownership, and measurable business impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a multi-channel public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where possible for channels/studio/analytics: growth in email engagement, social reach, production volume, cost savings, reporting speed, or stakeholder adoption.
- Tighten wording and use stronger verbs: “Established NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio,” “Built analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery,” “Implemented governance and publishing standards to improve cross-department coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise ownership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video production language may duplicate older NACo roles; here, emphasize building institutional capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; produced/grew weekly advocacy video update; coordinated cross-team editorial calendar; improved publishing workflows and consistency.
- Add outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size/open rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated, publishing volume.
- Example rewrite: “Managed NACo’s daily digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution across communications, advocacy and program teams. Oversaw four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders, expanded a recurring advocacy video series, and improved publishing workflows to increase consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led digital communications across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry by emphasizing scaling/operationalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around leadership scope rather than repeating generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy content strategy,” “Audience and journey-based content planning.”
- Use parallel phrasing throughout; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with vague descriptors (“messaging”).
- Consider adding one higher-value leadership signal: “Enterprise web and content modernization” or “Digital operating model design.”
- If space allows, swap “multi-channel communications leadership” for “Integrated web, email, social and video leadership” to align with recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header summary and Core Competencies; “content strategy” would feel stronger and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and current strategic value rather than listing generic tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to Coding/Technical Implementation or drop it if lightly used.
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of a bare list: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and alignment with the rest of the CV.
- If you want a stronger version: **Drupal (enterprise web modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Topline Skills entry listing the same platforms; keep one list broader and the other more impact/context-driven.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel inconsistent beside enterprise CMS platforms unless it supports a specific project narrative.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more specific, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Group and simplify: “HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- Drop version numbers unless required by the role; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used for Drupal front-end builds, tagging, lightweight serverless functions, and deployment automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so keep this item focused on coding/implementation tools rather than broader systems.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more implementation-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack, Teams.”
- Put strongest/relevant tools first based on recent work: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, then project/collaboration tools.
- Consider adding a light qualifier if accurate: “used to build intake, approvals, publishing, and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Cut weaker/older tools if space is tight; keeping 6–7 tools is stronger than listing every platform ever used.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if they weren’t central to systems design, they add little differentiation.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email operations are already emphasized in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS match: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep it platform-only unless you can support outcomes elsewhere; e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • audience segmentation / campaign automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader communications claims; “Member Engagement” is more specific if that reflects actual use.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this line is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and make the optimization language more specific.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard design**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO/performance analysis** to keep this item tool- and execution-focused.
- Change **Dashboarding** to **KPI/dashboard design** or **executive reporting dashboards** for stronger phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to impact in recent roles rather than here (e.g., analytics infrastructure supporting 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding.”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-stage buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and multimedia delivery.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, publishing volume, audience growth, or efficiency gains from new workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; distinguish this item as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you specify this was the initial team/process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground scope and outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active line: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and member engagement.”
- If possible, add one metric or output count: number of projects supported, episodes produced, or programs/policy teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing digital/media leadership here; later NACo roles already cover web, video, newsletters, and team leadership in much stronger detail.
- “Multimedia production” may feel repetitive unless tied specifically to podcast or program-support content.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia strengths already covered elsewhere.
